title: Problem brief
description: Data for one problem brief page. The renderer fixes the layout; this file holds only the content.

title.description: Short name for the page, two to five words. Becomes the artefact title.

subject.description: One plain sentence naming what this brief is about and who must act on it.

generated.description: Date the facts on this page were last re-derived from the tree. Not the date the page was first written.

source.description: What produced these findings, in plain English. e.g. 'the implementation review on the importer branch, 2026-09-11'.

context.description: One paragraph the reader needs before entry one. Optional. Never a summary of the entries.

decisions.description: The brief proper. One entry per root cause, not per finding.

mechanical.description: Unambiguous fixes already applied. Listed so the reader knows they were handled, never asked about.

outstanding.description: Agreed work not yet done. Kept apart from the decisions.

diagramTheme.description: Theme passed to embedded archify pages. 'auto' follows the reader's theme.

id.description: Stable citation handle. Q-1, Q-2, … Never renumber an existing entry.

title.description: The problem as a headline, in plain English. No identifiers standing alone.

problem.description: Part a. One or two sentences naming what is wrong. No preamble, no background.

brief.description: Part b. Two to eight sentences on why that matters, in the reader's terms.

evidence.description: Part c. Verified evidence grounded in real things: code lines, documents, prior findings.

unwound.description: Part d. How it works today and why that is wrong — or the target state where there is no defect.

solutions.description: Part e. The first is the recommendation and must carry recommended: true.

rolledUp.description: The individual findings this entry absorbed, each named in plain English with its identifier trailing.

assumptions.description: Claims not yet proven, stated outright, each saying what would settle it.

status.description: open — needs your ruling. decided — you chose a way forward, it has not been carried out yet. complete — the chosen way forward has been carried out and the entry is closed; that covers work landing, a question being answered, or scope being cut, whichever the chosen option was. superseded — the problem went away or was overtaken, and nothing was carried out.

chose.description: The id of the chosen solution.

note.description: The reasoning, in the operator's words where they gave it.

decision.description: Which option was chosen and why. Set when the ruling is made, and kept afterwards.

resolution.description: What actually happened. Required once status is complete — a closed entry without proof is a claim, not a record.

date.description: The day it was carried out.

note.description: What was done, in one or two sentences. Say it in the same plain terms as the problem.

evidence.description: Proof it happened: the commit, the pull request, the test that now covers it, the ruling that cut the scope.

differs.description: Where what landed differs from the option that was chosen, and why. Leave out when it matches.

kind.description: What sort of thing is being cited.

ref.description: The citation itself: path:line, a spec path, a commit hash, a run identifier.

note.description: What this citation shows, in one sentence. Required in practice — a bare path proves nothing.

url.description: Optional link, where one exists and the reader can open it.

verified.description: False marks the claim as unproven on the page. Say in the note what would settle it.

now.description: How the thing actually behaves today.

whyWrong.description: Why that behaviour is a problem. Use where there is a defect.

target.description: The state we want instead. Use where there is no defect, only a gap.

kind.description: mermaid renders natively in the page. archify embeds a rendered archify page. svg inlines a self-contained file.

caption.description: What the reader should take from the picture. Not a title — a claim.

file.description: kind=archify: published path of the rendered archify page, e.g. diagrams/q1-flow.html. kind=svg: local path of the .svg file to inline.

spec.description: kind=archify: path of the archify JSON this page was rendered from. Keep it so the picture can be edited rather than redrawn.

archifyType.description: kind=archify: which archify renderer produced the page.

embed.description: kind=archify: how the drawing is carried. 'inline' (the default) puts the whole drawing inside the page, so the page stands alone and needs nothing published alongside it. 'file' references it as a companion file, which keeps the page small but only works where the publishing tool can carry companion files — pass the companion paths the renderer prints. Prefer inline unless the page is getting large.

height.description: kind=archify: force a fixed frame height in pixels. Leave it out — the renderer works the height out from the drawing's own proportions, which is what stops it being cropped.

id.description: Short handle, unique within the entry.

work.description: How much work, in real terms. Not a t-shirt size on its own.

risk.description: What could go wrong if we pick this.

steps.description: Optional ordered steps, where the option is not self-evident.

summary.description: What was wrong and what was done, in one sentence.
The work, named so the reader knows what it delivers.

blockedBy.description: The entry id this waits on, where it waits on a ruling. e.g. Q-2.
